purpose: test whether the human-AI axis, and specifically the component that carries its causal effect, overlaps the refusal direction on the same model (Li et al. 2026, arXiv 2603.24543)
refusal_construction: difference of means, harmful minus harmless, sign toward refusal, per layer, Arditi et al. 2024

capture_modes.reply: mean over a 48-token greedy assistant turn

primary_readout: stripped |cos(axis_residual, refusal)| at layer 13, with PC1 of the dissolution_a0 cloud removed from BOTH vectors, axis-kept printed for each
layer_13_rule: the RAW cosine at 13 is quoted once as a sanity number with the house p95 0.994 beside it, and is never evidence

nulls.own: 200 label shuffles, refusal rebuilt, |cos| against ours, p95
nulls.random: E|cos| of random directions at d=2560

decision_rule.ruled_out: stripped |cos| at 13 inside this run's own null p95 AND raw |cos| at 27 and 33 below the house p95
decision_rule.live: stripped |cos| at 13 above this run's null p95 AND raw |cos| at 27 or 33 above the house p95
decision_rule.intermediate: inside one null and outside the other: report the fraction, claim nothing stronger

cross_readout_outranks: if section 5's AUCs disagree with the cosine, the AUCs carry the verdict: the paper's claims are made of orderings, not of cosines
behavioral_arm: section 6, matched-norm refusal steering at fractions -1.0 / 0 / +1.0 of dose 4.0 on the 10 held-out identity questions, scored by a fresh unsteered pass
unscoreable_rule: an arm whose math canary fails or whose text is degenerate is reported as incoherent, never as a null
